clue.text: Start of pitching really upset bad sailor?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of pitching
someone really upset is angry

explanation.surface: A seasick sailor is thrown into a state by the boat's pitching.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a poor seaman; the question mark flags that 'bad' here means criminal rather than incompetent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a seafarer who robs ships, a sailor who is bad in the moral sense.

clue.text: Co-operate in theatrical performance with dance

blocks.note: a play is a stage drama
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Working together on a stage show that includes dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to help or work along with others.

clue.text: Hold in high regard, in particular

definitions.note: a noun here, as in 'in every particular'

blocks.note: first meaning: to esteem someone
second meaning: a detail or point, as in 'in that regard'

explanation.walkthrough: 'In particular' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is a link and 'particular' is a noun meaning a detail.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for esteeming someone and a noun for a point or aspect of something.

clue.text: Has meal consumed by sailors, characteristic of boat to China?

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed and sits inside it

blocks.note: tars is a crossword staple for sailors
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats a meal with the crew aboard a ship to China.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the 'slow boat to China', a byword for a very long, slow journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness or slowness is what the proverbial slow boat to China is known for.

clue.text: Policy's revised about masculine sporting event

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are put in a new order
about means surrounding, so the reworked letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine

explanation.surface: A sports body has rewritten its policy on male athletes at a big competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympics are the international multi-sport games held every four years.

clue.text: Object after guiding editor's work

indicators.note: placing one thing after another sends the first-named piece to the second position

blocks.note: to guide is to lead
an article is an object or item

explanation.surface: A protest raised following some guidance about an editor's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, to protest, but is a noun meaning a thing; 'after' puts it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article, or leader, is a newspaper's editorial opinion piece, often written by the editor.

clue.text: He seizes power that is symbolic in Commonwealth country

definitions.text: that is symbolic in Commonwealth country
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the thing itself

indicators.note: to seize something is to grab hold of it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: he refers to a male
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A man grabs power in a Commonwealth nation, a symbolic act.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commonwealth country is Canada, whose flag bears the leaf of this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple leaf is Canada's national emblem, appearing on its flag.

clue.text: Progress with it on Greek island, it's said

indicators.note: something said is heard rather than read, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: being 'it' or 'in' both mean fashionable
Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Advances made with something on a Greek island, as rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Rhodes' spoken sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances or headway made, as in making inroads into a problem.

clue.text: Small and convenient mixed drink

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
handy means conveniently useful

explanation.surface: Describing a cocktail that is small and easy to make.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer, a British pub favourite.

clue.text: Female easily carried instrument in black box

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
something light is easy to carry
a recorder is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: A woman carries a portable musical instrument inside a black case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests the cockpit kit; it is the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's flight recorder is popularly called the black box, though it is usually orange.

clue.text: Big island in a lake in mountainous land

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: Austria is an Alpine country
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A traveller describes a large island in a lake somewhere in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an island inside a lake; in fact 'a lake' is the piece placed inside the Alpine country.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is often described as the world's largest island, or the smallest continent.

clue.text: Garment worn for warmth in mostly chilly area

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: parky is British slang for cold
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A coat you put on to keep warm when out somewhere cold.
explanation.walkthrough: PARKY is informal British for chilly; losing its last letter leaves PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket designed to keep the wearer warm.

clue.text: Developing book about section of party

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
re means concerning
a political party has left and right wings

explanation.surface: A book is being written about one faction within a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble that is brewing is building up or developing, as tea does when it steeps.

clue.text: I caught African animal in country with greater latitude

blocks.note: taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the eland is an African antelope

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts of catching an African beast somewhere far to the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greater latitude' sounds like more freedom, but it means lying further from the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: This North Atlantic island nation lies just south of the Arctic Circle, far north of most countries.

clue.text: Extreme pieces of literature put together in volume

indicators.note: only the pieces at the two extremes are kept, so the middle stretch is thrown away

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bits of books gathered together into one tome.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the opening three and closing two letters of the long word and join them up; 'volume' looks like a book, but it is a measure of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit measuring capacity, one thousand cubic centimetres.

clue.text: Showing fierce determination and unusual grit, is he?

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man displays ferocious resolve and remarkable grit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigerish describes behaving like a tiger: fierce, aggressive and relentless.

clue.text: Not completely sure, though tester made another assessment

indicators.note: the run of words is not used completely, only a stretch lying inside them

blocks.note: a run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: An examiner, unsure of a result, reviewed it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Having rethought something, one has reconsidered it, judging it a second time.

clue.text: Olympian tragically poisoned

indicators.note: a tragic turn wrecks things, so these letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete has met a tragic end by poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests a Games athlete, but it means one of the gods living on Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon, Greek god of the sea, was one of the twelve Olympian deities.

clue.text: For French form of address, is entering Parisian street name? Au contraire!

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this word slips between the other two
French for on the contrary, telling the solver to run everything the other way

blocks.note: rue is French for street
taken as written
nom is French for name, kept French by the Parisian setting

explanation.surface: A puzzle about French etiquette and street names in Paris, closing with a French flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: Both street and name are rendered in French because of 'Parisian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsieur is the French courtesy title for a man, equivalent to Mr or sir.

clue.text: He lost his wife taking her up, so awfully

indicators.note: something done awfully is botched, so these letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A widower lost his wife while leading her upwards, and it went terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface retells the myth: leading Eurydice up from the underworld, he looked back and lost her.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus, the legendary Greek musician, lost Eurydice forever by glancing back before they reached daylight.

clue.text: Excessively consuming salt is forbidden

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: too means to excess
an old salt is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A health warning: eating too much salt is not allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is not table salt but a sailor, as in old salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboo describes something prohibited by custom or social convention.

clue.text: Large numbers turned up after sailing ship docked in port

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its end
in a down clue, turning something up flips it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing vessel
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: Crowds appeared once a sailing vessel moored in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests mooring, but it means cut short. The port is the English city in the West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a historic English port city on the River Avon near the Severn estuary.

clue.text: Blunder when playing music ruined performance, ultimately

indicators.note: something ruined has been wrecked, so these letters are scrambled
ultimately points to the very end of a word, keeping its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of performance

explanation.surface: A musician's slip ended up spoiling the whole concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing music' sounds like a concert, but the definition is a mistake in a game such as snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty stroke in billiards or snooker where the cue slips off the ball.

clue.text: One way of working that includes bygone painting technique

indicators.note: something that includes another holds it inside

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MO is modus operandi, a method of working
bygone means past

explanation.surface: An artist's working method incorporates an old-fashioned approach to painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the application of paint in thick layers so brush or knife marks stand out.

clue.text: Prop in second team

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a crew is a team, as in a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A rugby prop forward playing for the reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' suggests the rugby position but is short for propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propeller is also called its screw, from its spiral blades.

clue.text: Declaration in church before line is added to English worship

blocks.note: the vow made at a church wedding
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A churchgoer makes a solemn declaration, with some English line of worship added.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to adore or revere them excessively, as if worshipping an idol.

clue.text: Less expensive – reduced by a penny? Hurrah!

indicators.note: something reduced by an amount has that amount taken away

blocks.note: costing less
taken as written, removed
p is the abbreviation for a penny, removed

explanation.surface: A shopper celebrates a price cut of a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Not just the penny but 'a' as well comes out of the longer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheer is a shout of joy or encouragement, the sort of thing hurrah expresses.

clue.text: Something done about match, perhaps, that makes one happy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a deed is an act
a match is one example of a light

explanation.surface: An achievement in a sporting match that leaves a person happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game, but here it is a thing you strike to give a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means very pleased, a strong form of being glad or joyful.

clue.text: Trade was switched away from West

indicators.note: things switched around are moved to different positions, so these letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Commerce once diverted from the Western world.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading eastward is travelling towards the east, the direction opposite to west.

clue.text: Name on piece of neckwear snatched

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another sits after it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: a stole is a scarf worn around the shoulders
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A name tag on a scarf that has been grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the first piece after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen means taken unlawfully, which is what snatched goods have been.
